misconceptions.description: Jumping straight to polish in the capstone instead of carrying audience, structure, media, narration, citation, and access checks through
misconceptions.trigger: learner submits a themed deck that never states its purpose or passes a contrast check
misconceptions.feedback: Walk the full pipeline: purpose, structure, explanatory media, value-adding narration, verified citations, accessibility. Polish is last.

misconceptions.description: Submitting the final deck with no record of what changed and why
misconceptions.trigger: learner turns in the deck with no before/after or rejected-suggestion note
misconceptions.feedback: Attach a revision trail: the earlier version, the issue, the support used, and one suggestion you rejected with a reason.

misconceptions.description: Letting AI assemble the entire capstone deck and submitting it as your own judgment
misconceptions.trigger: learner accepts an AI-built deck end to end without deciding anything
misconceptions.feedback: Use AI for bounded help on single moves; the capstone must show your decisions across the whole pipeline.
